summary_paragraph: Mr. Thompson, a right-handed male with composite Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphoma with CNS involvement, was admitted for his fifth maintenance cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. He reported stable symptoms, primarily intermittent visual floaters that typically improve post-treatment. He tolerated the infusion well, with mild nausea managed by ondansetron. Constipation developed during admission and responded to lactulose and stool softeners. His methotrexate level decreased to 0.22, and renal function remained stable with adequate hydration and urine alkalinization. A brain MRI showed no evidence of tumor recurrence, with a small T2-hyperintense frontal lesion unchanged and consistent with gliosis. He was discharged home in stable condition on oral leucovorin, docusate, senna, and ondansetron as needed, with instructions to restart aspirin and follow up for his next chemotherapy cycle.
